description: Paginate the notices API so bursts / post-downtime backlogs are not silently missed. Today run() calls fetch_notices(..., page=1) exactly once, so if more than one page of still-new notices exists between runs (after downtime, a state gap, or a posting burst), older-but-still-new posts on page 2+ are never seen -- the same 'notifications silently missing' family the prior round fixed for other causes. Add page-walking that fetches successive pages until a page yields no NEW (unseen) posts, or an empty/short page, or a safety page cap is hit; preserve the existing seen_ids dedup, sort order, and MAX_NOTIFY_PER_RUN capping exactly. Must remain correct and testable offline under INTEGRATIONS_ONLY.
steps: In bot.py, add a module-level constant near MAX_SEEN_IDS, e.g. MAX_FETCH_PAGES = 10, with a comment explaining it is a safety cap so a misbehaving/paginating-forever API cannot loop unbounded.

Add a new helper function fetch_all_new_notices(session, *, base_url, seen_ids, max_pages=MAX_FETCH_PAGES, timeout_sec=15.0) -> tuple[list[dict], list[int]] (or a small dataclass) that: starts at page=1; calls the EXISTING fetch_notices for each page; normalizes items via normalize_notice and filters id>0; accumulates all encountered current_ids (across pages) AND the normalized notices; stops paging when EITHER the raw page is empty, OR the page contained zero ids that are not already in seen_ids (i.e. no new posts on that page => deeper pages are older and also seen), OR max_pages reached. Return the combined list of normalized notices seen across fetched pages and the combined current_ids list. Keep the HTML-drift / JSON-parse RuntimeError behavior from fetch_notices unchanged (let it propagate).

Important semantics: 'stop when a page has no new posts' relies on the API returning notices in a stable order where newer items are on earlier pages. Since ids are NOT monotonic and page 1 may include pinned notices, compute 'new on this page' as any normalized id not in seen_ids. Document this assumption in the function docstring. The safety cap guarantees termination regardless.

In run(cfg), replace the single 'raw_items = fetch_notices(get_session(), base_url=cfg.base_url, page=1)' + normalize + current_ids block with a call to fetch_all_new_notices, using the seen_ids that run() already computes. NOTE the ordering: run() currently computes seen_ids AFTER fetching (for the new-post-diff) but BEFORE that it also handles init/first-run using current_ids. Restructure carefully so: (a) test_latest and init/first-run paths still get the full current notices/current_ids (for these paths, call fetch_all_new_notices with seen_ids=empty set OR just fetch page 1 as before -- choose the minimal change that keeps those paths' existing behavior: init/test-latest only need page 1's current view, so it is acceptable to still fetch page 1 for those and only paginate on the real notify path). Prefer: compute the stream/seen_ids first, then for the normal notify path paginate; for init_only/first-run/test_latest keep fetching page 1 only (their behavior must not change).

Preserve existing downstream logic verbatim: new_posts = [p for p in notices if p['id'] not in seen_ids]; sort by (post_date, id); MAX_NOTIFY_PER_RUN cap taking the most recent cap items with the [INFO] message; seen_ids update = _prune_seen_ids(seen_ids | set(current_ids)). current_ids must now be the union across all fetched pages so pruning/seen bookkeeping covers everything fetched.

Add offline tests in tests/test_bot.py (new TestCase class, e.g. FetchAllNewNoticesTests and PaginationRunTests) following the existing _FakeSession + mock.patch pattern: (1) a fake that returns scripted page responses keyed by the 'page' value in the POSTed json, then assert fetch_all_new_notices walks pages 1..N and stops correctly; (2) all-new across 3 pages then an empty page -> all collected; (3) page 2 has zero new (all already in seen_ids) -> stops without fetching page 3; (4) max_pages cap halts a would-be-infinite API; (5) an end-to-end run() test using mock.patch.object(bot,'fetch_notices', side_effect=<scripted pages>) asserting notify() receives posts drawn from multiple pages and state seen_ids includes ids from all pages. Do NOT hit the network; mock fetch_notices or session.post as the existing tests do.
Run python3 -m py_compile bot.py and python3 -m unittest discover -s tests; confirm the 40 pre-existing tests still pass plus the new ones.
acceptance_criteria: bot.py defines fetch_all_new_notices and run() uses it on the normal notify path; page=1-only behavior is retained for init/first-run/test-latest paths.
Pagination stops on empty page, on a page with no new (unseen) posts, or at MAX_FETCH_PAGES, and never loops unbounded.
seen_ids/current_ids bookkeeping and MAX_NOTIFY_PER_RUN capping behavior are unchanged for a single-page scenario (regression-safe).
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests passes, including new pagination tests that would fail if pagination were reverted to single-page.
findings: Added MAX_FETCH_PAGES=10 constant and fetch_all_new_notices(session, *, base_url, seen_ids, max_pages, timeout_sec) -> (notices, current_ids). It walks pages 1..N via the existing fetch_notices, normalizes/filters id>0, dedupes items repeated across pages (pinned notices), and stops on an empty page, a page with no unseen ids, or the max_pages cap. HTML-drift/JSON RuntimeError propagates unchanged. run() now uses it on the normal notify path only; test-latest/init/first-run still fetch page 1 only via the pre-existing upfront fetch_notices(page=1) call. NOTE: on the normal notify path run() therefore fetches page 1 twice (once upfront for the shared init/test view, once inside the walker) - this is the minimal restructuring the plan explicitly permits ('acceptable to still fetch page 1 for those'); the new PaginationRunTests assert requested_pages accordingly (e.g. [1,1,2,3]). Downstream new_posts diff, (post_date,id) sort, MAX_NOTIFY_PER_RUN cap, and _prune_seen_ids(seen_ids | current_ids) preserved verbatim. Added 8 offline tests (FetchAllNewNoticesTests x7, PaginationRunTests x2 -> actually 6+2). Verified: py_compile exits 0; all 48 tests pass (40 pre-existing + 8 new). New multi-page tests would fail under single-page behavior (they assert posts drawn from page 2+ and seen_ids covering all pages).
